title: Azure MCP Server
summary: Start Microsoft's Azure MCP server via npx and let the agent work with Azure storage, Monitor logs and Cosmos DB using your az login.
description: The Azure MCP server gives an agent tools for Azure Blob storage, Azure Monitor queries and metrics, and Cosmos DB NoSQL data. The old Azure/azure-mcp repository is archived; development moved to microsoft/mcp, which is where this setup comes from.
It authenticates with the Azure Identity SDK, so run az login first and the server acts as you. It has no documented read-only flag, so use an Azure role that only grants read access.
useWhen: Run a Log Analytics query while chasing an incident
List blobs in a storage container
Query a Cosmos DB container for sample documents
Check metrics for a misbehaving app

mcp.name: azure
access: Azure resources your signed-in identity can reach
Can write data and run queries according to that identity's roles

example.prompt: Query the app-prod Log Analytics workspace for errors in the last hour and group them by operation name.
example.result: 214 errors: POST /checkout 131, GET /cart 58, POST /login 25. The checkout errors started at 14:12.

faq.question: How does it sign in?
faq.answer: Through the Azure Identity SDK. Log in with the Azure CLI first; for containers, tenant, client ID and client secret variables are used.

faq.question: How do I stop it from changing things?
faq.answer: Give the identity a reader-style Azure RBAC role. The project recommends least-privilege roles rather than a server flag.

access: Reads and may change Azure resources your identity can use
